concepts.title: Water Cycle and its Processes
concepts.definition: The continuous circular movement of water across the atmosphere, land, and oceans through changing physical states.
concepts.key_idea: Water continuously changes form and circulates among land, air, and ocean systems.
question_patterns: what is the water cycle and how does it function
explain the stages involved in the continuous movement of water
describe how water circulates between land, atmosphere, and oceans
identify the processes involved in the water cycle
define precipitation and its role in water circulation

solution_steps.explain: Solar radiation heats surface water causing it to vaporize into atmospheric vapour.
Cooling atmospheric water vapour condenses to form clouds.
Condensed droplets fall back to land or ocean as rain, snow, or sleet.

concepts.title: Calculation of Ocean Water Salinity
concepts.definition: The mass of dissolved salt contained in a given quantity of water, standardized per thousand units of water mass.
concepts.key_idea: Determining dissolved salt amount using salinity in grams per thousand grams of water.
question_patterns: calculate the amount of salt in grams present in a given mass of water
find the mass of dissolved salt in water of known salinity
determine how much salt is in water given salinity and total mass
what is the weight of salt in water with specified salinity
compute the total dissolved salt from salinity and water weight

solution_steps.action: multiply salinity by total water mass
solution_steps.explain: Multiply the salinity rate per thousand by total mass of water

solution_steps.action: divide by 1000 to find salt mass
solution_steps.explain: Divide the scaled value by 1000 to get absolute salt mass in grams

concepts.title: Fresh Water Percentage Calculation
concepts.definition: Calculating available fresh water percentage by subtracting total saline ocean water percentage from hundred percent.
concepts.key_idea: Subtracting saline water percentage from 100 yields the percentage of fresh water on earth.
question_patterns: find the percentage of fresh water if ocean saline water is given
calculate available fresh water percentage from total water distribution
what is the remaining percentage of fresh water given saline percentage
determine fresh water proportion from total water percentage
compute fresh water percentage from saline ocean proportion

solution_steps.explain: Subtract the percentage of ocean saline water from total 100 percent to get fresh water percentage

concepts.title: Ocean Waves and Tsunamis
concepts.definition: Disturbances on the ocean surface causing water to rise and fall alternately, ranging from wind waves to massive seismic tsunamis.
concepts.key_idea: Winds create ordinary waves while seismic events under the sea floor trigger destructive tsunamis.
question_patterns: what are ocean waves and how are they formed
explain the causes and characteristics of a tsunami
describe how winds affect the size of ocean waves
what factors determine the height and destructive power of waves
how do underwater earthquakes generate massive tsunami waves

solution_steps.explain: Friction from winds blowing across the ocean surface causes water to rise and fall alternately.
Seismic movements like underwater earthquakes shift massive water volumes creating high speed tidal waves.

concepts.title: Mechanism and Utility of Tides
concepts.definition: The regular twice-daily elevation and recession of ocean surface water driven by lunar and solar gravitational pull.
concepts.key_idea: Gravitational forces create rhythmic tidal movements that assist navigation, fishing, and power generation.
question_patterns: what are tides and what causes them to occur
explain how high tide and low tide happen twice daily
describe the benefits of high tides for navigation and fishing
how does the gravitational pull of the moon produce ocean tides
what role do tides play in electricity generation and harbour entry

solution_steps.explain: Gravitational pull exerted by the sun and moon attracts earth surface water.
Water facing the moon rises into high tide while receding elsewhere creates low tide.
High water levels enable ships to reach harbours easily and bring fish closer to coasts.

concepts.title: Spring Tides versus Neap Tides
concepts.definition: Variations in tide height caused by linear alignment or right-angle positioning of the sun, earth, and moon.
concepts.key_idea: Linear celestial alignment produces high spring tides while orthogonal pull causes low neap tides.
question_patterns: differentiate between spring tides and neap tides
when do spring tides occur and why are they highest
explain why neap tides occur during quarter moon phases
how does the position of the sun and moon affect tide height
what causes maximum and minimum tidal ranges on earth

solution_steps.explain: During full and new moon phases, sun, moon, and earth align in a straight line, generating highest spring tides.
During first and last quarter moons, sun and moon pull at right angles, resulting in lower neap tides.

concepts.title: Ocean Currents and Thermal Effects
concepts.definition: Continuous directional flows of ocean surface water driven by temperature variations across polar and equatorial regions.
concepts.key_idea: Warm and cold ocean currents redistribute thermal energy and create optimal global fishing grounds.
question_patterns: what are ocean currents and how are warm and cold currents classified
explain the difference between warm currents and cold currents
how do ocean currents affect the climate of coastal areas
why are meeting zones of warm and cold currents rich fishing grounds
give examples of famous warm and cold ocean currents

solution_steps.explain: Warm currents originate near equator and move poleward, while cold currents carry polar water toward lower latitudes.
Currents moderate land temperatures and mixing zones create rich feeding grounds for marine life.
